chunks: I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about wiping over the two feet, and he said: It is what Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام brought down.
And with this chain, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ṣafwān, from al-ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad, from one of the two عليهما السلام,
He said: I asked him about wiping over the two feet, and he said: There is no harm in it.

And al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from al-Ḥakam ibn Miskīn, from Muḥammad ibn Sahl,

He said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: Sixty or seventy years may pass over a man while Allah has not accepted from him any salat (prayer). I said: How is that? He said: Because he washes what Allah has commanded to be wiped.

And al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUbaydillāh informed me from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Abī Hammām, from Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام,
Concerning the obligatory wudu (ablution) in the Book of Allah, he said: Wiping [is required], and washing in wudu (ablution) is for cleanliness.
Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah,

He said: He said to me: If you were to perform wudu (ablution) and make the wiping of the foot into washing, then inwardly hold that this is among the obligations, that would not be wudu (ablution). Then he said: Begin with wiping over the two feet, and if washing occurs to you and you wash them, then wipe after that, so that the last of that may be the obligation.

As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd al-Madāʾinī, from Muṣaddaq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام,

Concerning a man who performs the whole wudu (ablution) except his feet, then enters the water with them fully, he said: That suffices him. So this report is to be understood in the state of taqiyyah; but when there is choice, it is not permissible except wiping over them, as we have explained.
As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbdillāh narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ,

He said: I wrote to Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام asking him about wiping over the two feet, and he said: Wudu (ablution) is by wiping, and nothing is obligatory in it except that; and whoever washes, there is no harm. His statement عليه السلام, 'and whoever washes, there is no harm,' is to be understood as cleanliness, because he had mentioned before that and said: Wudu (ablution) is by wiping, and nothing is obligatory in it except that. If washing had also been part of wudu (ablution), it would have been obligatory. He clarified that in the narration of Abī Hammām which we presented earlier, where he said: In the obligatory wudu (ablution) in the Book of Allah, there is wiping, and washing in wudu (ablution) is for cleanliness.
As for what Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār narrated from ʿUbaydillāh ibn al-Munabbih, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUlwān, from ʿAmr ibn Khālid, from Zayd ibn ʿAlī, from his fathers, from ʿAlī عليه السلام,

He said: I sat to perform wudu (ablution), and the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم came when I began the wudu (ablution), and he said to me: Rinse the mouth, draw water into the nose, and clean the teeth. Then I washed three times, and he said: Two times may suffice you for that. Then I washed my two forearms and wiped my head twice, and he said: One time may suffice you for that. And I washed my two feet, so he said to me: O ʿAlī, pass between the toes; do not pass through with fire. So this report agrees with the generality, and it came in the context of taqiyyah, because what is known, in which no doubt stirs, from the doctrines of our Imams عليهم السلام is the القول of wiping over the two feet, and that is more famous than for doubt or suspicion to enter into it. What clarifies that is that the transmitters of this report are all from the generality and men of the Zaydiyyah, and what they alone transmit is not acted upon, as has been explained elsewhere.

key_terms.الرِّجْلَيْنِ: the two feet, the body part under discussion in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.الْغَسْلُ: washing, mentioned here as distinct from the obligatory wiping
key_terms.الْفَرِيضَةِ: the obligatory ruling established in religion
key_terms.الْمَسْحِ: wiping as the obligatory act over the feet in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.لِلتَّنْظِيفِ: for cleanliness, not as the obligatory element of wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: In Shia hadith, is the obligation in wudu for the feet washing or wiping?
ai.summary: This passage gathers several narrations and authorial clarifications establishing that in wudu (ablution), the obligation concerning the feet is masḥ, not washing. Reports suggesting washing are explained either as referring to cleanliness rather than the obligatory act, or as cases of taqiyyah in contrast to the well-known teaching of the Imams عليهم السلام.
